questions.stem: In a reaction, the total energy needed to break all bonds in the reactants is 1500 kJ, and the total energy released when forming all bonds in the products is 1800 kJ. What is the enthalpy change?
questions.explanation: Delta H = energy to break bonds - energy released making bonds = 1500 - 1800 = -300 kJ. The negative sign indicates more energy is released making new bonds than is needed to break old bonds, so the reaction is exothermic. In exothermic reactions, bond making releases more energy than bond breaking absorbs.

questions.stem: Hydrogen reacts with chlorine: H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl. Given bond energies: H-H = 436 kJ/mol, Cl-Cl = 242 kJ/mol, H-Cl = 431 kJ/mol. Calculate the enthalpy change.
questions.explanation: Bonds broken: 1 x H-H (436) + 1 x Cl-Cl (242) = 678 kJ. Bonds made: 2 x H-Cl (2 x 431) = 862 kJ. Delta H = 678 - 862 = -184 kJ/mol. The reaction is exothermic because more energy is released forming H-Cl bonds than is absorbed breaking H-H and Cl-Cl bonds.

questions.stem: Why is breaking chemical bonds always an endothermic process?

options.text: Because atoms naturally repel each other when bonds are broken
Because energy must be supplied to overcome the attractive forces holding atoms together
Because the products have lower energy than the reactants
Because broken bonds release their stored energy

questions.explanation: Chemical bonds represent attractive forces between atoms (shared electrons in covalent bonds, electrostatic attraction in ionic bonds). Energy must be put in to pull the atoms apart against these attractive forces. This is always endothermic. Conversely, forming bonds is always exothermic because energy is released when atoms come together.

questions.stem: The combustion of methane is: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O. Bond energies: C-H = 413, O=O = 498, C=O = 805, O-H = 464 (all in kJ/mol). What is the enthalpy change?
questions.explanation: Bonds broken: 4 x C-H (4 x 413 = 1652) + 2 x O=O (2 x 498 = 996) = 2648 kJ. Bonds made: 2 x C=O (2 x 805 = 1610) + 4 x O-H (4 x 464 = 1856) = 3466 kJ. Delta H = 2648 - 3466 = -818 kJ/mol. The large negative value confirms combustion is highly exothermic.

questions.stem: A student calculates the enthalpy change for a reaction using bond energies and gets -250 kJ/mol. The experimentally measured value is -235 kJ/mol. Why might these values differ?

options.text: The student made a mathematical error
Bond energies are average values across many compounds, so they do not exactly match specific molecules
The experiment must have been done incorrectly
Bond energy calculations always give exact results

questions.explanation: Bond energy values given in data tables are averages taken from many different compounds. The actual energy of a specific C-H bond, for example, varies slightly depending on the molecule it is in. Therefore, calculations using average bond energies give approximate values that may differ from experimentally measured enthalpy changes.
